_: BLACK GLASS — nest_1. Re-run with: tools/shot.sh --seq=tools/seq/nest_1.json
__: Ten captures: every one of the four screens, every teaching beat, and BOTH of
___: this level's gates in BOTH configurations — the trading wall before and after
____: its lever (shots b and c) and the slag gate before and after its own (g and h).
_____: Contact-sheet them with: tools/grid.sh shots/nest_1_sheet.png 5 2 shots/nest_1_[a-j]_*.png

_: GOTCHAS, all of them paid for by earlier levels. A teleport puts the TOP-LEFT of
__: the body on the tile's top-left, so a 22 px human's feet land in the row below:
___: aim one row ABOVE the row she should stand on and let her drop. Teleporting onto
____: the exit tile completes the level and the capture lands on the hub, so the last
_____: shot stands five tiles short of it. A bare {"settle": n} step is a NO-OP —
______: dev_capture.gd only reads `settle` off a `scenario` or a `teleport`; idling on

_: AND ONE THAT IS THIS LEVEL'S OWN: a lever is tripped by CONTACT, and SwitchTrigger
__: re-arms every 0.45 s (27 frames) while a body is still inside its box. So the way
___: to photograph a thrown switch is to land on it with a SHORT settle and teleport
____: off again before it re-arms: {"teleport": [10,11], "settle": 20} throws it exactly
_____: once. Settling 30 there would throw it twice and photograph the level unchanged.

_: SCREEN A — THE GLASS SHELF. Spawn at (3,12) on obsidian, under four tiles of
__: headroom, with the whole of World 5's vocabulary in one frame: nest_shard in the
___: pit at cols 5-6, nest_vein glowing in the walls, obsidian_hot banding the rock it
____: touches, the nest_ledge mezzanines at row 9 and the nest_chain hanging off each.
_____: settle 210, not 90: the level-title card is still up at 90 and covers the room.

_: SCREEN A — THE TRADING WALL, GROUP 1 ON. This is how the level starts. The wall
__: at col 17 runs floor to roof and has two doorways in it: the HIGH one at rows 7-8
___: is switch_block_a_off and is standing open, the LOW one at rows 11-12 is
____: switch_block_a_on and is a wall. The lever is on the floor at (10,12) with both
_____: of them in frame, which is the whole of beat 2: one screen, one glance.

_: SCREEN A — THE TRADING WALL, GROUP 1 OFF. The same frame, one throw later: the
__: wall has become a door and the door has become a wall. Nothing else in the level
___: changed and nothing was lost — a nest_ledge mezzanine runs to the sill on each
____: side and a chain drops off each mezzanine, so whichever half of group 1 is solid,
_____: both rooms are connected both ways. That is why this beat is free.

_: SCREEN B — THE CORRIDOR EAST, at mark 'pit_b_east' (35,12). The second shard pit
__: at cols 33-34 is behind her, two tiles wide like the first, so both are crossed at
___: the human's measured 3-column displacement. Niches in the roof, a flyer patrolling
____: row 8 that never comes down to row 12, and the mouth of the hole away east.

_: SCREEN B — THE HOLE, at mark 'shaft_head' (43,12). The cap stops here; cols 44-45
__: are open for fourteen tiles. The nest_chain at col 45 is the way back UP and is
___: load-bearing twice over — it is what the slag gate takes away two screens later,
____: and it is what keeps the shaft's foot a legal room in every configuration. The
_____: two-tile shelf beyond it is a 2-tile gap, inside the human's measured 3.

_: SCREEN D — THE FOOT OF THE HOLE at (44,26), where the fall ends. The corridor is
__: two tiles tall from col 41 east, which is what lets one column of switch block
___: seal it: a two-tile plug in a five-tile corridor would be a step, not a gate. The
____: nest_crust at col 46 with a heart behind it is the level's one breakable and is
_____: off every hop — tools/solver/sim.gd breaks nothing, so a breakable is a wall to
______: the gate and anything behind one has to be optional.

_: SCREEN D — THE SLAG GATE, GROUP 2 OFF. Beat 4, and the reason it is one screen:
__: switch_b at (37,26), the way she came in at col 43 standing OPEN six tiles east
___: of it, and the mouth of the furnace at col 28 standing SHUT nine tiles west. One
____: lever, two gates, fifteen tiles apart, all three in this frame.

_: SCREEN D — THE SLAG GATE, GROUP 2 ON. The same frame, one throw later, and both
__: ends of it have changed at once: the plug at col 43 has closed behind her — and
___: what it closes off is not a corridor, it is the chain, the whole way back up to
____: the first half of the level — while the mouth of the furnace at col 28 has opened.
_____: The level said this would happen before she threw it: she got here by falling

_: SCREEN C — THE FURNACE. Teleported onto pad_frog at (33,26) a row high so she
__: falls INTO its box, then west past the opened gate: every capture from here on is
___: the frog. The pad is EAST of the last gate on purpose — by the time anyone is
____: inside the furnace they are already the frog, and the crack at col 28 rows 22-23,
_____: whose sill is a 3-tile step, is a door to the frog and a wall to Kaya in every
______: configuration. That crack is the only reason a room with no lever in it is legal.

_: SCREEN C — THE WAY OUT, on tread 3 at (8,17), five tiles short of the exit —
__: standing ON it would end the level and land the capture on the hub. The whole
___: climb is in frame: three treads of nest_ledge in 3-tile steps, which is the frog's
____: MEASURED ceiling and one more than the human's, so the pad is load-bearing rather
_____: than decoration. The floor's cap is obsidian_hot the whole way across and the
______: exit's own shelf is plain obsidian: down here the cold rock is the way out.
